claims.text: The baseline TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy.
TiVNbTa has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
TiVNbTa has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K and around 30% strain.
The proposed intervention is to add 3–5 at.% W to TiVNbTa.
Adding W will enhance solid-solution strengthening in TiVNbTa.
Adding W will stabilize the BCC phase of TiVNbTa at high temperature.
Tungsten's high melting point and low diffusion rate will impede high-temperature dislocation activity.
W addition will reduce high-temperature dislocation climb and motion in TiVNbTaW.
Reduced dislocation mobility and increased solid-solution strengthening will improve high-temperature yield strength.
TiVNbTaW may exceed 450 MPa yield strength at 1273 K.
TiVNbTaW will maintain ductility close to 40% strain at 1273 K.
TiVNbTaW will sustain efficient heat transfer between W and CuCrZr.
The prediction is intended to apply around 1273 K and at strains up to approximately 30–40%.
NbMoTaW and NbMoTaVW exhibit weak temperature dependence of yield strength from 600 to 1600 °C and retain yield strength above 400 MPa at 1600 °C.
Strength–ductility tradeoffs and brittle W-enriched BCC phases are possible in W-containing alloy design.
Identically processed TiVNbTa and TiVNbTaW controls will be compared in tensile and compression tests at approximately 1273 K, with phase stability monitored during thermal cycling.
Failure to obtain at least a 30% yield-strength improvement at 1273 K, or observation of significant phase destabilization or incompatible ductility loss, will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions limit loading to 30% strain, whereas the predicted ductility is close to 40% and the boundary is variously stated as 30–40%, leaving the upper loading boundary inconsistent.
